subject: Business
title: Growth Hacking Origins
description: A short lesson to help you apply Growth Hacking Origins.

hook.text: Sean Ellis coined 'growth hacker' in 2010 for people obsessed with one thing: growth.

buildup.text: Growth hacking uses creative, low-cost experiments instead of big marketing budgets.

discovery.text: Airbnb hacked Craigslist by letting hosts cross-post listings. Free distribution, millions of eyes.

twist.text: The term got overhyped. Every marketer rebranded as a growth hacker without changing anything.

climax.text: The real lesson survived the hype: test ruthlessly, measure everything, double down on what works.

punchline.text: Growth isn't magic. It's disciplined experimentation.

quiz.question: What is the core principle behind growth hacking?
options: Low-cost creative experiments focused on growth

details.summary: Growth hacking, coined by Sean Ellis, applies experimental, data-driven techniques to achieve rapid user growth on limited budgets. Early examples include Hotmail's email signatures, Dropbox's referral program, and Airbnb's Craigslist integration, where product features drove growth instead of
details.whyItMatters: Growth hacking demonstrated that startups could grow without traditional marketing budgets by embedding growth mechanisms into the product itself. This insight changed how startups approach customer acquisition and made product-led growth mainstream.
takeaways: Growth hacking uses product features and data experiments to drive rapid user growth
Hotmail, Dropbox, and Airbnb all grew through product-embedded growth mechanisms
Sean Ellis coined the term to describe marketing skills specific to startup constraints

faq.question: What was Dropbox's famous growth hack?
faq.answer: Dropbox offered 250MB of free storage for every friend a user referred. Both the referrer and the new user received free space. This cost Dropbox almost nothing but created a viral referral loop that grew the user base from 100,000 to over 4 million in 15 months.

faq.question: Is growth hacking still relevant or has it been replaced by other approaches?
faq.answer: The specific term is used less, but the principles evolved into product-led growth. The core idea that growth should be driven by product experience and data-driven experimentation rather than brand advertising remains central to modern startup strategy.
